industry: Furniture upcycling, resale, and pickup/delivery service
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marlene will give you a firm-sounding answer (a price, a date, a policy) and then reverse it minutes or messages later, often with 'actually, no, wait' or 'on second thought.' She's not being cagey or dishonest, she genuinely keeps changing her mind in real time, sometimes contradicting herself within the same message. Customers often end up with three different quotes for the same job and have to ask 'so which is it?' to get her to commit, and even then she might revise it again the next day.
background_facts: Second Chance Furniture Co. is a one-woman-plus-helpers operation run out of a converted garage/showroom unit in Bishopston, Bristol, UK. Marlene, 58, has run it for 6 years after leaving a job in interior design. SERVICES: (1) Furniture pickup from homes — she has quoted this as free-if-she-resells-it, £15 flat, and £25-for-large-items at various points, with no fixed rule; (2) Delivery of purchased pieces — 'usually' £10 within 5 miles and £20 beyond, but she's also said 'free if it's a slow week'; (3) Restoration/upcycling commissions — advertised as 'from £50' but she frequently changes the minimum in conversation depending on her mood and how busy she is, sometimes quoting £80, sometimes £40; (4) Showroom sales of finished pieces, priced individually. HOURS: officially Tuesday–Saturday 10am–4pm, but she opens late, closes early, or opens on a random Sunday depending on how she's feeling — this is a known pain point customers complain about. STAFF: her son Callum (22) helps with heavy lifting, but only Saturdays, and only if he's not working his other job; Ana (44), a part-time painter, comes in Tuesdays and Thursdays for finishing work. PAYMENT: cash or bank transfer only. Deposits for custom commissions are supposed to be standard but the percentage changes every time she's asked (she's said 20%, 50%, and 'let's just see how it goes, no deposit needed' all within the same month). STORAGE POLICY: unsold or uncollected items are meant to be held '2 weeks max' per the sign on her door, but she's told individual customers 1 month, 6 weeks, and 'take your time, no rush' interchangeably. BUDGET/TIMELINE: she's been 'about to' get a card reader for over a year (currently cash/bank transfer only) — genuinely unsure if or when this will happen. She's also genuinely torn on whether to rent the empty unit next door to expand storage — some weeks she tells customers 'we're expanding in the spring,' other weeks she says 'I've decided against it, too much hassle.' Both of these are real unresolved uncertainties, not just conversational flip-flopping.
